units: pixels (x right, y down, origin top-left of the 1920x1080 frame), seconds

camera.motion: static (no pan/shake: background plate built from many frames is sharp, props do not move)
camera.view: side view, roughly horizontal camera facing a wall; animals walk left/right parallel to the image plane
camera.perspective_note: Floor recedes to the wall; the dog walks nearer the camera than the cat (dog paws touch floor at y~1061-1070, cat paws at y~1017-1023, dog occludes cat). Pixel scale differs slightly between the two lanes; horizon row unknown (camera looks roughly level). If the horizon were at image centre y=540, the dog lane would be ~10% nearer (scale ratio (1066-540)/(1020-540)=1.10). Treat as 2D unless a question needs better.

cat.description: black-and-white (tuxedo) cat with white paws/socks and an untextured grey head; tail raised; smaller animal
cat.occluded_by: dog (cat passes BEHIND the dog); heavily hidden ~frames 29-35
cat.pace_px_per_frame_note: nose (bbox_x1) is linear in time on visible frames: slope 17.76 px/frame, rms 0.7 px

dog.description: brindle (brown striped) dog with white paws and an untextured grey head, head lowered (sniffing); larger animal, nearer the camera

side_table.description: wooden slatted side table (orange-brown) at the right, with a lower shelf; partly cut by the right image edge
side_table.note: right end cut at x=1919; front of dog overlaps table in frames 0-~8

table_lamp.description: lamp on the table: white pleated cone shade + dark brown tapered wooden base

vase.description: blue-and-white porcelain vase standing on the table at the right (the real one, the larger/right of the two)

vase_reflection.description: mirror image of the vase, left of it, inside the mirror (not a real object)

floor_mirror.description: tall rectangular mirror with light wood frame leaning on the wall behind the table

dog_starts_walking.note: dog torso nearly at rest at frame 0 (steps ~1-4 px/frame over frames 0-3), then speeds up

dog_reaches_cruise.note: torso steps ~18-25 px/frame between frames ~16 and ~33

dog_slows.note: steps drop to ~10-16 px/frame by frames 38-44 and ~0.5-2 px/frame at frames 47-49 (dog nearly stopped at the end)

cat_walks_whole_clip.note: steady pace, ~17.8 px/frame to the right; no start/stop inside the clip

cat_nose_meets_dog_head.note: cat bbox_x1 (917) reaches dog bbox_x0 (913); blobs merge from frame 23

centres_cross.note: dog torso_cx equals cat fitted bbox_cx
